item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q009_heme_bundle_fold_not_homology","answer":"No. SCOPe 2.08 places them in three separate superfamilies within the Heme-binding four-helical bundle fold, f.21 (SUNID 81344): transmembrane di-heme cytochromes, f.21.1 (81342); fumarate reductase respiratory complex transmembrane subunits, f.21.2 (81343); and respiratory nitrate reductase 1 gamma chain, f.21.3 (103501). Their class is f, Membrane and cell surface proteins and peptides (56835).\n\nThus, their shared architecture is a fold-level relationship, not a single homologous superfamily or family. Families group more closely related proteins within superfamilies; superfamilies express inferred common ancestry, whereas shared fold or class alone does not. Separate superfamilies mean SCOPe does not establish common ancestry across these groups, not that distant ancestry is disproved. Heme binding and similar membrane helices do not justify transferring specific respiratory-complex roles, substrate specificity, or detailed mechanisms between them. A cross-superfamily structure may suggest an architectural template, but reliable residue correspondence and functional transfer require independent sequence/profile, detailed structural, and biochemical evidence.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope__search_scop","mcp__scope__get_scop_node","mcp__scope__list_scop_children","/api/v1/releases/current","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=Heme-binding+four-helical+bundle&mode=auto&limit=20","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/81344","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/81344/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/81344/children?limit=100"]}]}
